P1.evidence: Nothing from a setter or an application was read back at any point — this is the only call in the batch where the rep never referenced prior notes, and it showed later when he had to ask what the prospect did for a living. The frame was the usual three parts plus next steps: 'where you're at in your fitness journey, where you're trying to get to, what's kind of missing in between, and then we can create a game plan and figure out some next step from there.' Agreement taken with 'Does that all sound good?' and the open question ran: 'What do you feel we could potentially help you with?'

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch. Height, weight and age asked. Training week asked and walked through session by session. Diet asked and walked through meal by meal. Injuries asked and then properly clarified: 'Any injuries or health concerns, anything that's going to inhibit working out at all or limit movement?' followed by 'But right now, they seem to be fine, just to clarify.' Work was asked, though 38 minutes in and prefaced with 'I forgot to ask you', and the sitting-versus-standing question ran. The gap is that the prospect's active medical picture — a GLP-1 agonist, cardiologist-managed cholesterol medication and a pre-diabetic A1C — was all volunteered in the first eleven minutes and never asked about or returned to. Sleep and energy were never asked, and the prospect had volunteered persistent fatigue.

P3.evidence: The bridge and the ladder both ran: 'What's the motivation behind this all for you?' then 'so live healthy, but for what reason do we want to live healthy?' That produced travel with his wife, future grandchildren and, later, staying independent of his children. The reflect-back was clean and the prospect improved on it: 'It kind of feels like you've just been lacking a plan this entire time' — 'Sure. Or like a road map... and a coach to show the road map.' The costly miss is that immediately after the grandchildren answer, the rep changed the subject to holiday destinations — 'Where do you guys travel? Like, what's the places you guys go to?' — and the deepest emotional line on the call was dropped and never picked back up. Nothing was asked about a physical thing he wants to do but cannot.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase on the call and the best P4 in the batch. 'What do you think was missing every time you tried in the past?' opened it. The rep then named the pattern rather than accepting the surface answer: 'I know you said part of falling off is because we don't see the results, but it really sounds like it's been such a consistent pattern. Like, you fall off for a little bit, something health happens, oh, I figured this out, and then you kind of figure it out, and then you fall off again. Why do we keep falling off?' And he ran the root-cause challenge properly: 'even if you're seeing results, there's going to be a tendency to fall off, right? ... what needs to happen in order for us to be consistent with this? Not just the next six months, but the next six years.' The prospect named the gap himself as a road map plus a coach.

P5.evidence: Run and extended: 'if we don't get something consistent, what does the next 5, 10, 15 years look like if we don't find something that we can be consistent with?' The answer was strong — the seesaw, progressive muscle loss and the fear of dependence on his children — and the rep amplified it once: 'if we don't have that consistency, like it's just gonna go down and down and down.' Then nothing. No 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', and no line in the sand at any point on the call. The consequence material surfaced here is exactly what would have answered the price objection 40 minutes later and it was never referenced again.

P6.evidence: The commitment read was taken before the price and came back unambiguous: '1-10, 1, this is the dumbest thing I've ever heard... 10, holy crap, this is exactly what I need' — 'A 10 out of 10.' The belief question was then run twice after the price and confirmed again: 'finances aside... Do you really feel like everything that we covered ultimately can get you into the shape that you're wanting to get into?' The scripted go-all-in question was replaced by a framing about Trevor being selective rather than a direct 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in', which is why P6b is partial. The intent of the phase — a genuine yes before presenting — was met.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected, so step 1 is a miss and steps 2-4 were unreachable. The call ended with the rep texting his own number so the prospect could contact him after shopping competitors.

objection_plays.detail: The isolation ran and ran well, twice — 'finances aside, do you really feel like everything that we covered ultimately can get you into the shape that you're wanting to get into?' — and both times the value was confirmed. The situation probe ran: 'is it a matter of, you know, we just don't have access to the six grand right now? Or what's your situation specifically?' After that the play stopped. The should-versus-how reframe was never used. The permission question was never asked. Not one of the six financial-picture questions ran — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no credit, no investments. Most significantly, the break-it-up move never ran at all: this is the only call in the batch where no payment plan was offered, to a prospect whose stated blocker was the size of the single figure and who had just rated the offer 10 out of 10. The rep instead ran a future-retrospective close, which produced an initial yes and then a full retraction — 'I take back what I said' — and he closed the call less than a minute later.

The strongest OE trigger in the batch and the prospect quantified it himself: 70% inclined toward kettlebells, with the remaining 30% being 'the concern in the back of my mind about injury.' The rep isolated it correctly — 'outside of the concern about injuries, is there any other concerns... keeping you from being less than 100%?' — and then answered it with product mechanics rather than the play: light starting weights, video form checks, the mobility protocol, plus Trevor's shoulder-surgery story and his own shoulder and ankle recovery. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain frame, no bridge, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. It worked commercially — the prospect went to 10 out of 10 — but it worked by way of unqualified safety assertions ('it's like impossible to injure yourself', 'it becomes harder and harder and harder to get injured'), which is flagged separately.

'Maybe I just need, you know, time to explore maybe other programs' is a think-about-it in substance. Not one move was run. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal' — which he had already answered yes to twice and which was sitting right there. No 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is.' No 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started.' The rep closed the call instead.

Script gap — the prospect with no market reference point at all. 'You're the first person I spoke with. And so I have no, I have zero idea. So even talking about, you know, the numbers.' He was not comparing against a cheaper alternative; he had no alternative in mind and therefore no way to judge whether $6,000 was reasonable. Nothing in the playbook pre-frames the number, establishes what one-to-one coaching from a category-leading practitioner costs, or gives the rep a way to keep a comparison-shopper engaged. He walked out to go and build the anchor himself.

Script and product gap — the prospect on an active GLP-1 agonist. His entire framing was 'while the iron is hot, you know, with the GLP, let's hit the iron', and his goal was muscle preservation during drug-driven fat loss. After the opening minutes the rep never mentioned tirzepatide again, offered no protocol for training or eating alongside it, and pitched a consolidated eating window that runs against the protein-prioritisation his prescriber requires. This is a defined and growing prospect segment arriving with high intent and a hard deadline, and there is nothing in the script or the offer for it.

notes: Discovery and root cause were the best in the batch and the money phase was the worst: the rep confirmed value twice, established the blocker was the lump sum, and then never offered instalments at all — the only call here where that happened. Second coaching point: he had a 10 out of 10 and a fully surfaced consequence frame (dependence on his children, progressive muscle loss) and referenced neither when the price landed. The call was abandoned roughly sixty seconds after the first real retraction.
